title: NTS Bilingual Social Media Content and Weekly Reporting Workflow — User Behavior Patterns
goal: Demonstrate the end-to-end NTS social media content production workflow — from the monthly content plan through Claude Design, Canva, and Buffer — and the weekly performance reporting workflow — from native platform analytics through the branded NTS weekly report template — completed within a single Claude chat session.
context: As Marketing Manager for Native Translation Services (NTS), a certified translation, interpretation, notarization, and apostille company based in Austin, TX, I manage the full social media content production and performance reporting cycle. This session covers two interconnected workflows completed within a single Claude chat session. The first is a social media graphic production workflow: starting from the NTS monthly content plan, using Claude to build detailed design prompts or templates, generating initial graphics via Claude Design, refining them in Canva, and scheduling the final posts across multiple platforms using Buffer — including carousel (multi-slide) posts. The second workflow is the weekly performance reporting cycle: pulling native analytics data from Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and Google Business Profile, organizing the metrics with Claude, and updating the pre-established NTS branded weekly report Word template. Both workflows demonstrate Claude's role in reducing manual effort, standardizing quality, and enabling batch content operations at scale.
occupation: Marketing Specialist, BluShark Digital / Marketing Manager, Native Translation Services

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes, I demonstrated the workflow I’ve developed in a couple of strategic steps that facilitates the way I produce mass content and my reporting system

Step 1.step_name: Review the NTS monthly content plan and identify graphics needs
Step 1.step_action: Open the current NTS (Native Translation Services) monthly social media content plan and identify which posts require custom graphics or visual assets for the week. Determine the content type for each post (single-image graphic or carousel/multi-slide post), the copy and key message, and the platform(s) where it will be published (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok). Use Claude to organize and confirm the visual content brief for the batch.

nodes.label: Introduce NTS workflow goal
nodes.detail: Introduces the NTS (Native Translation Services) content workflow demo, noting that a lot of the content is bilingual English/Spanish for NTS's Hispanic-audience focus in Austin.

nodes.label: Preview the two demo tasks
nodes.detail: Explains they will demonstrate building one simple graphic and then a more complex multi-slide carousel post.

nodes.label: Open a fresh Claude chat
nodes.detail: Opens a new Claude chat to begin the content-plan and graphics workflow.

Step 2.step_name: Generate graphic prompts or templates with Claude and send to Claude Design (repeats)
Step 2.step_action: Use Claude to draft detailed visual prompts or design templates based on the content brief from Step 1. Prompts should specify layout, text overlays, color palette (Navy #223D73, Red #A62631, Light Gray #F2F2F2), imagery style, and platform dimensions. For carousel posts, generate a prompt for each individual slide, maintaining visual consistency across the set. Send the approved prompts to Claude Design to generate the initial graphics.

nodes.label: Start carousel idea, request prompt
nodes.detail: Starts a second, more complex content idea in the same chat -- a multi-slide carousel -- noting she barely needs to restate brand details since Claude already has the established brand awareness; asks Claude to generate the carousel prompt and sends it straight to Claude Design.

nodes.label: Return per-slide guidance
nodes.detail: Claude Design returns per-slide guidance (colors, typography, logo placement) for each carousel page; she notes Claude Design doesn't generate stock photography, which she'll add manually afterward.

nodes.label: Review Claude's per-slide prompt for Claude Design

Step 3.step_name: Export Claude Design graphics to Canva and finalize (repeat)
Step 3.step_action: Download or export the graphics generated by Claude Design. Import them into Canva as base assets. Apply final refinements: adjust typography, fine-tune layout alignment, replace any placeholder elements, and ensure brand compliance with NTS color standards. For carousel posts, finalize all slides as a single Canva presentation or multi-page design, ensuring visual consistency across slides. Export all finalized graphics at full resolution, ready for publishing.

nodes.label: Paste Claude's carousel prompt into Claude Design
nodes.detail: Copies the per-slide carousel prompt generated by Claude and pastes it into Claude Design to create the new carousel project.

nodes.label: Create new carousel project
nodes.detail: Because the carousel is too large for the already-exported single-post Canva project, Claude Design creates a new project labeled 'Native Translation Carousel.'

nodes.label: Confirm all 14 pages in Canva
nodes.detail: Sends the carousel to Canva and confirms all 14 pages (English and Spanish covers, five body slides each, and a closing slide) came through correctly, ready as a baseline for manual touch-ups like adding photos.

Step 4.step_name: Schedule and publish posts via Buffer
Step 4.step_action: Log into Buffer and create a new post for each item in the batch. Upload the finalized graphic(s) for each post, paste the approved caption, and select the target platform(s). For carousel posts, upload all slides in the correct order within a single Buffer post. Set the publish date and time for each post based on the NTS content calendar schedule. Use Buffer's batch scheduling feature to queue multiple posts in sequence. Review all scheduled posts in the Buffer queue before confirming.

nodes.label: Show Buffer content calendar
nodes.detail: Shows the Buffer content calendar used to schedule NTS posts across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and Google Business Profile, noting LinkedIn is posted manually since Buffer's LinkedIn integration has been unreliable.

nodes.label: Download finished graphics from Canva
nodes.detail: Downloads the finished English and Spanish graphics from Canva, each auto-labeled by client and language.

nodes.label: Paste caption and attach graphics
nodes.detail: Pastes a pre-drafted English caption into a new Buffer post and attaches the graphic to each target platform.

nodes.label: Apply platform-specific edits
nodes.detail: Removes the phone number from the Google Business Profile version (adding the website link via the 'Learn more' field instead), removes the plain-text URL for Instagram since captions aren't clickable there, and trims hashtags down to Instagram's 5-tag limit.

nodes.label: Set schedule and publish
nodes.detail: Sets the publish schedule to Monday at 10:30am and schedules the post across all selected platforms.

Step 5.step_name: Pull weekly platform insights and compile raw performance data
Step 5.step_action: Access the native analytics sections for each active NTS platform -- Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and Google Business Profile -- and extract the key weekly performance metrics for the reporting period. Metrics include: reach, impressions, engagement (likes, comments, shares/saves), profile visits, follower changes, and any platform-specific metrics (e.g., Google Business Profile calls, direction requests, website clicks). Use Claude to organize the extracted figures into a structured data table, ready to be entered into the weekly report template.

nodes.label: Introduce weekly reporting cycle
nodes.detail: Explains she'll show the weekly reporting cycle that follows content posting, for the reporting week of August 3-9.

nodes.label: Screenshot Facebook Insights
nodes.detail: In Meta Business Suite, opens Facebook Insights, uses Inspect to capture a full-size screenshot of the data summary, and renames the file 'Facebook report.'

nodes.label: Screenshot Instagram Insights
nodes.detail: Repeats the same Inspect-and-screenshot process for Instagram, saving the file as 'IG report.'

nodes.label: Export LinkedIn analytics
nodes.detail: Moves to LinkedIn Page Analytics, sets a custom date range matching the Meta window, and downloads the native Excel export since it is more complete than a screenshot.

nodes.label: Note TikTok skipped
nodes.detail: Notes that TikTok is skipped this week since she doesn't have account access from this laptop.

nodes.label: Screenshot Google Business Profile
nodes.detail: Opens the Google Business Profile performance dashboard, applies the weekly filter, and takes a direct screenshot of the visible chart after a custom screenshot attempt doesn't cooperate.

Step 6.step_name: Update the NTS weekly performance report template with current data
Step 6.step_action: Open the existing NTS weekly social media and digital performance report Word document (branded with Navy #223D73, Red #A62631, and Light Gray #F2F2F2). Enter the compiled weekly metrics from Step 5 into the correct fields and tables within the template. Update the reporting period header, any summary or highlight fields, and trend comparisons if present. Use Claude to review the updated entries for accuracy and flag any significant changes or anomalies worth noting. Export the final report as a formatted Word document.

nodes.label: Attach prior report and new screenshots
nodes.detail: Attaches the prior week's finished report ('NTS Weekly Report_Week 12.docx') to the same Claude chat alongside the four freshly captured screenshots/exports (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Google Business Profile).

nodes.label: Request new report, omit TikTok
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to build a new report following the same branded format for the current dates, explicitly telling it to omit the TikTok tracking section since there is no data for that platform this week.

nodes.label: Verify report accuracy and layout
nodes.detail: Checks the individual-posts sheet for a standout-post callout, verifies Instagram follower-growth math, confirms font/layout hierarchy matches the template, and checks all report pages before finishing.

nodes.label: Review Claude's finished report and download it
nodes.detail: Downloads the finished 'NTS Weekly Report Week 14' Word document.

nodes.label: Review report section by section
nodes.detail: Reviews the report section by section -- Work Completed This Week, per-platform Organic Performance tables with week-over-week percentage changes, and key observations -- confirming it correctly picked up the new Week 14 label and preserved the branded template structure; the session ends here.
